commits: 7962d85 fix: support halt-at-non-option with commands and positionals

criteria.text: With `parserConfiguration({ "halt-at-non-option": true })`, parsing `my-host ls` where host and cmd are positional arguments succeeds producing `host: "my-host"` and `cmd: ["ls"]`; options like `--verbose` are parsed if they appear before the first positional, and arguments after the first positional are left untouched

grader.evidence: Ran the issue's exact CLI against the built lib: ['my-host','ls'] → {host:"my-host", cmd:["ls"], verbose:0, _:[]} with no "Not enough non-option arguments" error. Options before the first positional are parsed: ['-v','my-host','ls','-l','--verbose','/tmp'] → verbose:1, host:"my-host", cmd:["ls","-l","--verbose","/tmp"] (the later --verbose/-l are left untouched inside cmd, not consumed as flags). Mechanism is sound: yargs-factory.ts:1990-1997 no longer forces 'populate--' on when halt-at-non-option is set (so halted args reach _ and thus command/positional handling), and command.ts:647-653 emi

criteria.text: A regression test reproducing the reported issue is added to the existing test suite

grader.evidence: test/command.mjs:1755 adds describe('halt-at-non-option') with 6 tests inside the existing suite, referencing the issue URL. The first test is a faithful repro of the report (usage('$0 <host> [<cmd>...]') + positional host/cmd + verbose count + .strict() + halt-at-non-option, args ['my-host','ls']); others cover options before the positional, halting after the first positional, a named command, and that '--' is not populated / is untouched when the config is off. Ran them in isolation: 6 passing.

criteria.text: The full existing test suite passes via `npm test`

grader.evidence: `npm test` completed with 838 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing, and the posttest `gts lint` + eslint checks passed. (Separately, `npm run test:esm` — not part of the graded test command — has 1 failing test, 'throws an error if commndDir() used in ESM mode'; it is unrelated to the diff, which touches only postProcessPositionals and the populate-- default, and looks environment-related.)
